name: Monaco

fees.name: Schengen short-stay visa (issued by French authorities, valid for Monaco)
fees.validity: Up to 90 days in any 180-day period
fees.applies: Nationalities not visa-exempt for the Schengen area
fees.notes: Monaco issues no visas of its own. It is not a Schengen member but applies Schengen rules via France: a Schengen visa valid for France also authorises entry to and stay in Monaco. Applications go through French consulates/France-Visas. EU Visa Code standard fee EUR 90 (adults), EUR 45 (children 6-12), free under 6. Visa-facilitation-agreement nationalities pay a reduced EUR 35 where agreements apply.

fees.name: Schengen short-stay visa (business purpose, via France)
fees.validity: Up to 90 days in any 180-day period
fees.applies: Nationalities not visa-exempt for the Schengen area
fees.notes: Same uniform Schengen fee; business and tourism use the same short-stay visa type C.

fees.name: Airport transit visa (type A, via France)
fees.applies: Nationalities subject to airport transit visa requirement
fees.notes: Uniform EU Visa Code fee applies to airport transit visas.

reciprocity_variations.note: EU Visa Code reduced rate for children aged 6-12; children under 6 free.

vfs.operator: VFS Global / TLScontact (varies by country, contracted by France)
vfs.note: France outsources visa intake in most countries to VFS Global or TLScontact; the published service fee is roughly EUR 22 plus taxes and varies by centre and local currency. Since Monaco entry uses French Schengen visas, this applies to Monaco-bound applicants.

free_visa_notes: Monaco has no visa regime or fees of its own. EEA nationals and all Schengen visa-exempt nationalities (e.g. USA, GBR, CAN and other Annex II countries) enter Monaco free with a valid passport/ID. Nationalities requiring a visa must obtain a French/Schengen short-stay visa (EUR 90) which is also valid for Monaco. There is no Monaco e-visa, visa on arrival, or eTA; ETIAS (when applicable to Schengen-exempt travellers) is an EU system, EUR 20.
